issues: "Her spells deal magic damage and scale with AP" overgeneralizes from E and R. Q also has supplied magic damage and AP scaling, but W is terrain with a zero proc true damage displacement interaction and no supplied AP scaling. Qualify this claim to the damaging spells supported by the evidence.
The AP learning focus is supported by the supplied damage formulas, but those formulas do not establish an optimal build.

core_coverage.answer_quote: When Rebirth is available, fatal damage turns Anivia into an egg.
core_coverage.reason: Explains both the availability condition and fatal-damage transformation.

core_coverage.answer_quote: She revives if the egg survives for a few seconds.
core_coverage.reason: Explicitly conditions revival on egg survival.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Anivia launches an ice projectile that damages and slows enemies along its path.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the projectile's path damage and slow.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Its explosion damages and stuns nearby enemies.
core_coverage.reason: Separately identifies the explosion's area damage and stun.

core_coverage.answer_quote: She can recast during flight to explode it early; otherwise, it explodes at maximum range.
core_coverage.reason: Explains manual early detonation and automatic maximum-range detonation.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Anivia creates a temporary ice wall that blocks movement through its terrain.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the movement-blocking terrain without claiming every movement ability is prevented from crossing.

core_coverage.answer_quote: The wall melts after a short time.
core_coverage.reason: Explicitly explains the wall's limited duration.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Anivia deals magic damage to a targeted enemy.
The damage doubles if the enemy was recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm.
core_coverage.reason: Explains both qualifying sources and preserves the fully formed storm condition.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Anivia toggles a persistent storm at a chosen location that repeatedly damages and slows enemies inside.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the toggle and chosen location. Persistent does not expressly promise unconditional or permanent maintenance.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Anivia toggles a persistent storm at a chosen location that repeatedly damages and slows enemies inside.
core_coverage.reason: Explicitly explains repeated damage and slowing within the storm.

core_coverage.answer_quote: The storm grows after activation, dealing more damage and applying a stronger slow at full size.
core_coverage.reason: Explains growth and both full-size enhancements.

conflicts.resolution: The draft appropriately avoids guaranteeing full health after revival. Preserve the distinction between health restored upon entering resurrection and current health upon completion; the supplied summaries differ in precision.
Use Riot and the detailed Wiki mechanics requiring a fully formed storm. The draft preserves this condition despite the abbreviated Wiki summary.
Use the detailed excessive-distance and cast-inhibiting crowd-control rules. The short summary does not establish that Anivia must stand inside the storm or that every disable interrupts it.

factual_risks: The overview's universal spell damage and AP-scaling claim requires repair.
Rebirth's visible-cue description is consistent with the supplied text, but this check does not verify the demonstration frames or current-client visuals.
Frostbite's bonus is determined at impact; the beginner wording does not guarantee the bonus merely because its mark existed at cast time.
Storm persistence is conditional on distance, mana and interruption rules. Their omission is acceptable here because the answer does not assert unconditional persistence.
Crystallize knockback speed remains explicitly unestablished.
UNAPPROVED and tentative-verification labels occur in metadata; they must remain outside card-facing text.
The frozen sources do not establish a current game patch or current-client behavior.
